headline: the direction is now MEASURED, and it is the opposite of what I registered: at block 47 the device gradient is INFLATED by about 18 % across essentially the whole block, not shrunk. And the block carries TWO separate defects, not one.
source: of3t-rebase landed amendment 14 within the hour: instrument_a_bundle.py:539-548 now emits device_norm, norm_ratio, cos and zero_model_rel, with an `identifiability` summary. Six A16 bundles, all scale_pair_bias=False (the trunk default this branch holds), same frozen reference 1d4ea9225f85, crop 64. Their median rel reproduces my independent recompute exactly at all four shared arms: 0.0121, 0.0192, 0.2013, 0.2386.
reading: BLOCKS 0 AND 23 ARE RIGHT. 94 % and 92 % of tensors have |norm_ratio - 1| < 0.05 AND cos > 0.99. Their two-to-four outliers are all attn_pair_bias tensors with reference norms of 5e-06 to 3e-04 -- precision on near-zero gradients, which is what the bar is meant to tolerate.

BLOCK 47 CARRIES A BLOCK-WIDE 1.18x INFLATION. Its norm_ratio deciles run 0.887 / 1.155 / 1.180 / 1.193 / 1.219: the middle half of the block sits inside +-1.6 % of 1.18, with cos 0.996-0.999. ZERO tensors are within 5 % of unit norm ratio. That is a common multiplicative factor, measured, not inferred.

THE ARITHMETIC CHECKS OUT. rel^2 = 1 + r^2 - 2rc with r = 1.180 and c = 0.9977 gives rel = 0.193 against the measured 0.2013. So block 47's failure is ALMOST ENTIRELY the magnitude, not the direction.

AND ONE TENSOR IS A SEPARATE, SEVERE DEFECT. 47.attn_pair_bias.layer_norm_a.weight has norm_ratio 32.556 and cos -0.5148 at a reference norm of 9.76e-03 -- 32x too large AND pointing the wrong way. That is the campaign's long-quoted worst tensor, and it is now characterised rather than merely named.
my_prediction_refuted: At pass 119 I registered the s_fp32_residual hypothesis with the prediction that block 47's gradient is SHRUNK -- per-block updates quantised away by a bf16 residual far larger than them, so norm_ratio << 1 with cos ~ 1. The cos half is right (0.998). THE DIRECTION IS WRONG: norm_ratio is 1.18, inflated. The hypothesis as registered is refuted, and the s_fp32_residual arm should be re-scoped or dropped rather than run to confirm a direction already measured against it.
what_a_scale_fix_would_buy: correcting the 1.18 alone takes block 47 from rel 0.2013 to sqrt(2-2c) = 0.068 -- a 3x improvement that still fails the 2.0e-02 median bar and still fails the 5.0e-02 per-tensor bar. So the inflation is necessary to fix and not sufficient.
correction_to_my_own_D36: D36 read rho ~ 1 as evidence of a COMMON multiplicative factor. rho is computed per tensor, so strictly it only shows the error is proportional to the reference WITHIN each tensor; commonality ACROSS tensors needed the norm_ratio spread, which D36 did not have. The measurement happens to support the stronger reading at block 47 -- the middle half sits inside +-1.6 % of 1.18 -- but D36 was entitled only to the weaker one.
